title: Dowry death vs cruelty - how courts distinguish the two charges
p1:
A wife dies after years of harassment. Is it automatically a dowry death case?

Many people assume every case involving a troubled marriage falls under the same charge. But courts look for specific facts before deciding.
p2: The surprising part: cruelty and dowry death are not the same offence. Cruelty usually focuses on harassment, abuse, or pressure faced by the woman during the marriage. Dowry death requires an additional connection — the death must be linked to dowry-related harassment happening soon before the incident.
p3:
Courts examine evidence such as complaints, witness statements, messages, financial demands, and the timing of alleged harassment. A history of cruelty may exist without proving dowry death. The key question is not only “Was she treated badly?” but also “Was the death connected to dowry demands?”

Knowing this difference helps people understand why courts may apply different charges in similar-looking situations.
